headline: High-risk workspace overlap: Replit Agent can write and exfiltrate code/secrets while mem0 has no documented isolation or verification boundary.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: mem0 is a knowledge-management component with no documented shared channel, while Replit Agent can read/write Repl files and act inside a workspace. A prompt-injection path exists only if mem0 outputs are manually copied or stored in shared files; no default direct bridge is documented, so this stays low.
conditions: IF mem0 outputs are copied into Replit workspace files as instructions, then prompt injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared file or paste workflow is introduced between the agents, then the attack surface increases.
mitigations: Keep mem0 outputs out of executable files.
Use a separate notes file for mem0 content.
Require human review before pasting mem0 text into Replit.
Add a prefix like 'untrusted summary' to imported text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to copied content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Replit Agent touches secrets, source code, and deployment configuration and has broad network egress; mem0 is a memory store with no stated data-class limits. If mem0 content is placed in the shared Repl workspace, Replit can read it and potentially transmit it, creating a realistic leakage path in default workspace use.
conditions: IF mem0 stores secrets or sensitive notes in Repl workspace files, then Replit Agent can read them.
IF Replit Agent sends workspace-derived context to external services, then leakage can occur.
mitigations: Do not store secrets in shared workspace files.
Move sensitive mem0 data to a separate vault.
Redact secrets before any handoff to Replit.
Review Replit network calls before running tasks.
requires-engineering: isolate the agents onto separate storage volumes.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Replit Agent has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and shell/network capabilities; mem0 is a knowledge-management system with no coordination or locking surface. If both operate on the same Repl workspace, concurrent writes and git edits can collide, and the profiles show no lock or optimistic concurrency mechanism to prevent corruption.
conditions: IF mem0 and Replit Agent target the same workspace directory, then write conflicts are possible.
IF both modify git state without an external lock, then repository corruption or lost updates can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Use git branches instead of shared main.
Check for file diffs before each write.
requires-engineering: add workspace locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Replit Agent can act on workspace content and modify code, while mem0 can supply remembered text that may be treated as context. If Replit consumes mem0 output without verification, mistaken or stale memory can cascade into code changes or deployment edits; the profiles do not show a built-in verification step.
conditions: IF mem0 output is fed into Replit Agent as authoritative context, then errors can propagate.
IF Replit Agent uses that context to edit code or deployments, then downstream impact expands.
mitigations: Require a human check before acting on mem0 output.
Ask Replit Agent to cite the source of each claim.
Compare mem0 output against the workspace state.
Limit mem0 to suggestions, not instructions.
requires-engineering: add automated verification against source files.

E_compliance.rationale: Replit Agent explicitly handles secrets and deployment configuration and has broad network egress, while mem0 is a memory system with no documented residency, retention, or deletion controls. If EU PII or regulated secrets are stored in mem0 and then used in Replit, the pair can create a compliance breach without any documented safeguard in either profile.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in mem0 and then copied into Replit, then residency/retention controls may be violated.
IF the operator relies on Replit for secret handling without a DPA or retention policy, then compliance risk increases.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Use synthetic or masked data for development.
Confirm retention and deletion settings before use.
Document a data-handling policy for the pair.
requires-engineering: obtain and enforce a DPA and residency controls.
